column1: # Kyrgyzstan, kg.default: the Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Kyrgyzstan, the Muftiate (muftiyat.kg), a likely majority
# (the state-recognised Hanafi muftiate; no mosque survey). Its calendar page, /kg/calendar/?start=&end= with the cookie
# point=<id> (the site's own locality picker), prints a table for each of its 115 localities for any range of dates; all
# 115 were captured for 2026 and 2027 on 12 Nov 2026 by the kg-muftiyat fetcher (tools/timetables/monitor/fetchers/
# muftiyat_kg.py), raw replies in archive/raw/monitor/kg-muftiyat/2026-11-12/, pinned in archive/tables/pinned/kg-muftiyat/
# 2026-11-12/. Terms: all rights reserved (the site's footer); robots.txt allows all; used only to fit and prove.
# The Muftiate prints the same month-day times every year (its 2026 and 2027 tables are equal day for day), computed on
# 2023's sun (CentralAsia.kt); so the 2027 rows repeat 2026's times on 2027's dates, Ramadan 1448 (8 Feb-10 Mar 2027)
# among them. Its "maghrib" is its own, 7 min after the "sunset" the page also prints (the M column); the page's header
# marks Fajr as also the start of the fast, so the Fajr column is also the end of eating (F+E).
# What the Ramadan proof rests on, said plainly (the review of 13 Nov 2026): the end of eating = Fajr is read from that
# column header alone ("Багымдат" with "Сухур*" under it, as "Шам" carries "Ифтар*"); the held page has no footnote
# for those asterisks (they are its only two), and no Ramadan (orozo) table of the Muftiate's is held, so an imsak it may
# print before Fajr in Ramadan would not be seen here. If it prints one, the app's end of eating would be after it. To
# capture before Ramadan 1448 (8 Feb 2027), with the owner's say on the route (the site's script builds
# One table year, captured once: every count of days below and in the stamp is 2026's table and its repeat on 2027's
# dates, from the one capture of 12 Nov 2026 (and the monitor's since); the majority is inferred, not surveyed.
# Points: the Muftiate gives no coordinates. Each locality's point is the one its own table is computed for, recovered
# from its 2026 table (KyrgyzLocalities.kt; within 3.7 km of the app's own point for each of the app's 32 Kyrgyz cities),
# and each locality is a unit there (ruling R44, as QMDB's places). Aravan's table is computed about 52 km south of the
# town: the town is a unit of its own (aravan-town), held to that table at the town's point.
# Split: the 2026 and 2027 tables of 58 localities (every other one by the Muftiate's id) are fit rows (the 2027 table
# repeats the 2026 one, so it is fit data too: the review of 12 Nov 2026); the other 57 localities' tables are held out.
# The app's own points: each of the app's Kyrgyz cities against the table of the locality whose unit holds it, held out
# (a fit locality's table read at another point, as the reach rows, kg-default-reach.tsv, read every table). Each
# locality's point was recovered from its own 2026 table, a held-out locality's too: what is held out is the margins.
# Shamaldy-Say's 2027 table is a re-capture: in the first, 25 Aug 2027 alone of all 115 x 730 days differed from the same
# month-day's other year (its sunset, Maghrib and Isha minutes later than 2026's);
# later the same day the calendar page and the documented API (/kg/api/v1/calendar/38/) both printed that day as 2026
# does. Both raw replies are kept (shamaldy-say-2027.html.gz, .recapture.html.gz). Against the first capture's 25 Aug the
# app would be minutes early at Maghrib and Isha. The owner accepted the re-capture as it stands on
# 12 Nov 2026. That the first capture's 25 Aug was the site's passing slip is our reading, not a thing the Muftiate
# said: it rests on one re-capture later the same day, in which the page and the API both agreed with 2026; and
# the monitor checks every new or changed capture of shamaldy-say-2027 against the engine, so a 25 Aug like the first
# capture's comes back as a never-early item. Aravan stays as it is (the owner, the same day): the table's own point
# and the town's unit held to that table, with the town's stated lateness.
# Leap years: the Muftiate prints a leap year's rows by day of the year (its 29 Feb is every other year's 1 Mar), the
# engine by month-day (fixedTableYear), so from 29 Feb 2028 to the year's end the app is a day behind the Muftiate's
# row: a start a minute or two before the Muftiate's where the time moves later day by day (Maghrib and Isha first,
# until June; Fajr later in the year), and an end of eating after it where Fajr moves earlier (until June). Which days
# and by how much is not yet computed.
# TODO before 29 Feb 2028 (logged 12 Nov 2026; the owner, the same day: leave the engine as it is until then and make
# the gap impossible to forget): a day-of-year mode in the shared engine's fixed-year mapping (DayComputer.fixedDay).
# The monitor says so on every run from 1 Dec 2027 (Horizons.DATED, "kg.default needs its 29 Feb 2028 handling") until
# the gate has read the Muftiate's own 29 Feb and 1 Mar 2028 at every locality, for Fajr, the end of eating, Maghrib
# and Isha, with nothing broken; docs/MONITOR.md, "Work by hand, by date", holds the steps. Until then prove reports
# the 2028 rows the monitor adds from Jan 2027, and under ruling R185 the first early one demotes kg.default.
# Before 12 Nov 2026 kg.default was fitted on one archived day at Bishkek (the homepage JSON's one day, the first rows
# below, the same times as the calendar's), with the year's own sun; its Dhuhr came a minute before the Muftiate's on
# about 170 days a year (the engine survey of 11 Nov 2026).
# Ruling R272 (the second trust audit's G29, 14 Nov 2026): every locality's point was recovered from its own 2026 table
# (KyrgyzLocalities.kt: sunrise, transit, sunset, the 18° dawn and the 16° dusk fitted to its printed minutes), and the
# 2027 table and every later capture repeat it day for day, so no locality's table is held out of the fit: what the
# split column holds out is the margins alone, which is no held-out proof of the times shown. The line below makes every
# pinned Muftiate table a fit table for every event, as Egypt's point-fitted months (R172) and Oman's are; the stamp's
# held-out days for kg.default are then none, and the Ramadan guard names all 116 units as checked in fitted rows only.
